beats.text: Zoom handled about 10 million daily meeting participants.
beats.note: Zoom's own post gives the maximum for the end of December 2019, free and paid, as approximately 10 million.

beats.context: In March 2020, Zoom said it had reached more than 200 million daily meeting participants, free and paid.

beats.note: Zoom counted daily meeting participants. NPR described the same figures as daily users, so the original post is the one to trust.
The post covered Zoombombing harassment, removal of the Facebook SDK from the iOS client on 27 March, and an apology for confusion over encryption.

beats.text: Zoom said it had fallen short.
beats.note: Eric Yuan wrote that the company had fallen short of the community's, and its own, privacy and security expectations.

beats.name: The feature freeze
beats.role: Announced on 1 April, effective immediately, with engineering moved to trust, safety and privacy over the next 90 days.

beats.text: Twenty times the participants, then a feature freeze.
